alias.danger_sentence: An alias carries data into another modeled access path; the security meaning depends on what receives it.
alias.attack_sketch: An attacker supplies a value at the source and it remains attached as it crosses the alias into a later operation.
checklist: Identify the value that is aliased.
Trace every consumer of the alias.
Check whether a later boundary constrains it.

alloc-size.danger_sentence: An allocation size is modeled because an attacker-influenced value can change memory consumption.
alloc-size.attack_sketch: A crafted size requests an unexpectedly large allocation, exhausting memory or triggering downstream bounds failures.
checklist: Find the origin of the size.
Check for an upper bound before allocation.
Check arithmetic for overflow or wraparound.

archive-entry.danger_sentence: An archive entry is modeled because its name or contents can cross a filesystem boundary.
archive-entry.attack_sketch: A crafted archive member uses traversal or link behavior to write outside the intended extraction directory.
checklist: Normalize and validate the entry path.
Reject traversal and unexpected links.
Extract with least privilege into an isolated directory.

buffer-size.danger_sentence: A size value controls how much memory an operation writes or reads.
buffer-size.attack_sketch: A caller supplies a count larger than the destination, turning a bounded-looking operation into memory corruption.
checklist: Find the source of the count.
Prove it fits the destination.
Check integer conversion and termination behavior.

buffer-write.danger_sentence: A write operation reaches a buffer without carrying an inherent proof that the destination is large enough.
buffer-write.attack_sketch: Input longer than the destination overwrites adjacent memory or truncates unexpectedly.
checklist: Identify destination capacity.
Check the write length before the call.
Confirm truncation or rejection is explicit.

code-injection.danger_sentence: Input reaches a dynamic code boundary where text can become executable instructions.
code-injection.attack_sketch: An attacker supplies syntax that is evaluated with the process's privileges.
checklist: Keep code and data separate.
Replace evaluation with a parser or allow-list.
Constrain the execution context if evaluation remains.

command-injection.danger_sentence: Input reaches command grammar where shell or process syntax can change what executes.
command-injection.attack_sketch: An attacker adds separators, substitutions, or flags that turn a value into a second command or alter the first.
checklist: Use a fixed executable and argument array.
Keep shell parsing disabled where possible.
Validate executable and argument domains.

concat.danger_sentence: Concatenation joins values before a later operation interprets the result.
concat.attack_sketch: An attacker-controlled fragment changes the meaning of the assembled string at its next boundary.
checklist: Locate the next interpreter or parser.
Keep structure separate from values.
Validate the resulting domain.

copy.danger_sentence: A copy transfers data across a boundary whose destination constraints must be checked by the caller.
copy.attack_sketch: A crafted value exceeds the destination's capacity or crosses an unintended ownership boundary.
checklist: Confirm destination capacity.
Check length and encoding assumptions.
Review ownership and lifetime rules.

deserialization.danger_sentence: Deserialization turns attacker-influenced bytes into structured values or objects.
deserialization.attack_sketch: A crafted payload invokes constructors, resolves types, or creates objects with behavior beyond plain data.
checklist: Use a data-only format when possible.
Select a safe loader and schema.
Bound size, depth, and resource use.

format-string.danger_sentence: A format string controls how another value is interpreted during output or logging.
format-string.attack_sketch: An attacker supplies format directives that read memory, write memory, or alter output behavior.
checklist: Keep the format string constant.
Pass external data as a value argument.
Check size and encoding limits.

insecure-temp-file.danger_sentence: Temporary-file creation is modeled because names, permissions, or placement can be attacker-influenced.
insecure-temp-file.attack_sketch: A race or predictable path lets an attacker read, replace, or redirect temporary data.
checklist: Use an exclusive, random creation API.
Set restrictive permissions.
Keep the file in a trusted directory.

insecure-tls.danger_sentence: A TLS or certificate operation is modeled because it controls whether a remote peer is trusted.
insecure-tls.attack_sketch: Weak validation or configuration lets an attacker impersonate the intended endpoint.
checklist: Validate the certificate chain and hostname.
Use current protocols and algorithms.
Do not disable verification for convenience.

ldap-injection.danger_sentence: Input reaches LDAP query grammar and can alter the directory search.
ldap-injection.attack_sketch: Special LDAP characters change the filter or distinguished name and broaden or redirect the query.
checklist: Use the library's escaping or parameter API.
Keep filter structure fixed.
Validate identifiers for their expected domain.

network-input.danger_sentence: Network input introduces data that remains attacker-influenced until a later boundary constrains it.
network-input.attack_sketch: A remote sender supplies a value that travels through the application into a sensitive operation.
checklist: Identify the protocol and trust boundary.
Validate shape, length, and encoding.
Trace the value to its consumers.

nosql-injection.danger_sentence: Input is interpreted as NoSQL query data or operator structure.
nosql-injection.attack_sketch: A crafted object or query fragment changes matching, filtering, or update behavior.
checklist: Separate query structure from values.
Reject unexpected operators and types.
Apply least-privilege database access.

open-redirect.danger_sentence: A caller-controlled destination determines where the application sends a user.
open-redirect.attack_sketch: A trusted origin redirects through an attacker URL, enabling phishing or token leakage.
checklist: Allow-list destinations or use local paths.
Normalize before comparing.
Do not reflect arbitrary URLs in redirect responses.

path-traversal.danger_sentence: Input participates in a filesystem path that should remain inside a trusted directory.
path-traversal.attack_sketch: Traversal segments, absolute paths, or links escape the intended root and reach another resource.
checklist: Resolve against a fixed root.
Reject traversal and unexpected schemes.
Check the resolved path before access.

prototype-pollution.danger_sentence: Input controls object keys that can modify shared prototype state.
prototype-pollution.attack_sketch: A crafted key such as a prototype path changes defaults or behavior for unrelated objects.
checklist: Reject prototype keys.
Use own-property checks and safe merge APIs.
Keep parsed data in null-prototype objects where appropriate.

redos.danger_sentence: A regular expression can consume disproportionate CPU on adversarial input.
redos.attack_sketch: A crafted string drives pathological backtracking and ties up the process.
checklist: Review nested ambiguity and backtracking.
Bound input length.
Use a linear-time engine or timeout where available.

regex.danger_sentence: A regular expression defines an input boundary whose accepted language may be broader than intended.
regex.attack_sketch: A crafted value matches an overly permissive pattern and reaches a later sensitive operation.
checklist: Test positive and negative boundary cases.
Anchor the pattern when matching whole values.
Apply a domain-specific parser where possible.

sql-injection.danger_sentence: Input reaches SQL grammar instead of remaining a bound data value.
sql-injection.attack_sketch: Quotes, operators, or comments in a crafted value alter the query's meaning.
checklist: Use prepared statements and bound parameters.
Keep identifiers and clauses allow-listed.
Review raw-query escape hatches separately.

ssrf.danger_sentence: A server-side request destination is influenced by a caller outside the server's trust boundary.
ssrf.attack_sketch: An attacker points the server at internal services, metadata endpoints, or unexpected hosts.
checklist: Allow-list schemes, hosts, and ports.
Resolve and validate redirects.
Use network egress controls as a second boundary.

template-injection.danger_sentence: Input is evaluated by a template engine as expressions instead of plain text.
template-injection.attack_sketch: Template syntax executes in the rendering context and may access data or capabilities.
checklist: Keep user input in data slots, not template source.
Use a sandbox only as defense in depth.
Escape for the actual output context.

transform.danger_sentence: A transformation changes representation while carrying the original trust relationship forward.
transform.attack_sketch: Validation is assumed after conversion even though the transformed value still encodes attacker control.
checklist: Identify what guarantees the transform provides.
Revalidate after decoding or conversion.
Trace the transformed value to its next boundary.

unsafe-reflection.danger_sentence: Input influences reflective selection of a class, method, or executable capability.
unsafe-reflection.attack_sketch: A crafted name selects a type or operation outside the intended allow-list.
checklist: Use explicit mappings instead of reflection.
Allow-list selectable types and operations.
Keep selected capabilities least-privileged.

untrusted-input.danger_sentence: The operation receives data whose origin is outside the current trust boundary.
untrusted-input.attack_sketch: A caller-controlled value travels through the program until a later operation gives it authority.
checklist: Name the source and trust boundary.
Validate at the point of use.
Trace all downstream consumers.

weak-crypto.danger_sentence: A cryptographic primitive is modeled because its strength may not meet the security property required by the caller.
weak-crypto.attack_sketch: An attacker exploits weak hashing, encryption, or protocol choices to recover or forge values.
checklist: Identify the property the primitive is meant to provide.
Use current, reviewed algorithms and parameters.
Check key, nonce, and mode handling.

weak-random.danger_sentence: A random value is used where an attacker may benefit from predicting it.
weak-random.attack_sketch: Observed outputs or predictable seeds let an attacker guess a token, identifier, or secret.
checklist: Use a cryptographically secure generator for secrets.
Inspect seed and state handling.
Check token length and lifetime.

web-input.danger_sentence: Web-facing input enters the application with an external trust origin.
web-input.attack_sketch: A crafted request value reaches a renderer, redirect, query, or command boundary.
checklist: Validate shape and size at the request boundary.
Encode for the output context.
Trace the value to sensitive consumers.

xpath-injection.danger_sentence: Input reaches XPath expression grammar and can change the selected XML data.
xpath-injection.attack_sketch: A crafted predicate broadens, bypasses, or redirects the XML query.
checklist: Use parameterized XPath APIs where available.
Keep expression structure fixed.
Escape and validate values for the XPath context.

xss.danger_sentence: Input reaches HTML or script output where the browser can interpret it as markup or code.
xss.attack_sketch: A crafted value breaks out of its intended context and executes in another user's browser.
checklist: Use context-aware output encoding.
Prefer safe DOM or templating APIs.
Apply a restrictive content security policy as defense in depth.

xxe.danger_sentence: XML parsing can resolve external entities from attacker-controlled documents.
xxe.attack_sketch: A crafted entity reads local resources or triggers server-side network requests during parsing.
checklist: Disable external entity resolution.
Use a hardened parser configuration.
Bound document size and expansion.
